specificities.definition: Inherent and irreducible unpredictability introduced by probabilistic machine learning models, whose outputs are non-deterministic and subject to statistical variance.

indicators.name: non_deterministic_outputs
indicators.description: Results that are not fixed and can vary between runs.

indicators.name: probabilistic_variance
indicators.description: Fluctuations in predictions and estimates based on statistical probability.

indicators.name: model_drift
indicators.description: Performance decay over time due to changing data patterns.

indicators.name: lack_of_reproducibility
indicators.description: The inability to consistently replicate AI-driven results.

indicators.name: data_dependency
indicators.description: High sensitivity to historical data quality and relevance.

indicators.name: non_linear_estimation
indicators.description: Complex relationships in cost and schedule that do not follow traditional linear paths.

indicators.name: opaque_outcomes
indicators.description: Algorithmic decision-making complexities that lead to results that are hard to explain.

indicators.name: dynamic_forecast_adjustment
indicators.description: The need to constantly update baselines as an indicator of underlying system instability.

management_frictions.name: baseline_erosion
management_frictions.description: Probabilistic variance forcing project managers to repeatedly adjust forecasts and commitments.

management_frictions.name: accountability_challenges
management_frictions.description: Opacity in outcomes making it difficult to assign clear responsibility for AI-derived decisions.
